identifier: flash/T387 (row closed under D054 as failed — the u6 hang; the fix and the full measurement set were completed on the follow-up row flash/T397; this file and the research doc are the report the Orchestrator asked for)
notes: The capture-budget investigation: does bounding total captures make the game finite, and at what cost? All numbers from the fixed binary (sha 5dbfd551); every figure with its denominator; controls ledger below.

method.rule: budget B = total stones captured over the whole game; a placement capturing k stones is legal iff budget_so_far + k <= B; budget lives in the state key (board, side, ko, passes, budget). Everything else (basic ko, suicide, passes, TIE=0 Chinese-area scoring at double-pass) is the WZO2/ADR-0020 semantics, mirrored from t386_engine.
method.instrument: src/t387_budget.zig (additive, measurement only; no engine/artifact/axiom edits)
method.base_table: data/oracle-3x3-v2.wzo2 (sha d79c17cd6fd00ba4608bdc5b86c9930a15d2a7050e2cdce07b0203f5aeaf7beb per T385) for the 3x3 hypothesis test

termination.claim: the budget-augmented game graph is a DAG — no directed cycles — hence every play terminates from every state, with no repetition rule at all.
termination.proof_sketch: budget is monotone non-decreasing along every play; a directed cycle would need constant budget; on a constant-budget cycle no capture occurs, so placements strictly increase the stone count and the board can never repeat, so no placement lies on the cycle; a pass-only cycle hits passes=2 and terminates. Game length <= 2(N+B)+1 plies.
termination.consequence: L == H everywhere under the budget rule — the bracket collapses structurally, no fixpoint ambiguity, no finisher needed.

state_space_cost.dense_key_multiplier: exactly (B+1) at every goban size — the budget is one small integer in the key; the table grows by (B+1): 4x4 table 396.5 MB (99,133,036 x 4 B entries) -> 3.57 GB at B=8, 9.9 GB at B=24.

4x4.trend: marginal states per budget level ~= 85M at 4x4, so the reachable multiplier grows roughly linearly in B: ~0.99 + 0.64B (4x4); dense multiplier is (B+1) regardless

state_space_cost.note: base = raw-key-space reachable from both fresh-start roots (matches the t386 census exactly: 3x3 73,758, 4x3 1,929,038); the published 98,999,934 (T380 10.1a) is the TABLE-entry count, a different measure

3x3_empty_root.note: stabilizes at +9 for B >= 6; the 3x3 table's own fresh-start empty-root entry is L==H==9, so the budget reproduces it

4x3_empty_root.note: OSCILLATES forever in {0,1,2,7,9,12} — no stabilization. The base bracket is [-1,12] and the PSK truth is +4 (RETRO_BRACKET); the budget value never converges and never equals +4

root_value_curves.reading: at 3x3 the budget reproduces a stable value (the determined root was already L==H); at 4x3 the value is B-arbitrary — this is the operator's absurdity relocated, not removed

hypothesis_3x3.framing: per-position fresh-start comparison vs data/oracle-3x3-v2.wzo2: V'(p) = budget-rule value of the subgame starting at p with the budget untouched (fresh-start semantics, matching T380 Q5's comparison class)
hypothesis_3x3.reading_L_eq_H: 21,126 fresh-start slots with L==H in the base table: 98.4% move at B=0, monotonically decreasing to 0.0% at B >= 24. The determined region is preserved once B >= 24 (at 3x3).
hypothesis_3x3.reading_L_lt_H: all 3,204 bracketed slots collapse to single values (DAG theorem), all inside the old bracket for B >= 24 — BUT the individual values are B-dependent and do NOT converge:

L_lt_H_value_drift.note: 39-51% of the bracketed slots change value between consecutive budget steps; the values oscillate within the bracket. The budget does not resolve the bracket — it replaces the honest [L,H] with an arbitrary B-dependent number. Raw per-slot data (B=24/32/48/64) in untracked/T397-brackets-drift/; reproducible via the committed brackets mode.

B24.note: 100% of the L==H slots match PSK (mismatch 0); among the 3,204 L<H slots, 1,224 (38.2%) match PSK — fewer than the pinned basic-ko value's 78.8% (T380 Q5)

3x3_root.note: a zero-capture optimal line exists (value +9) at every B >= 6; max grows with B — optimal lines exist using every capture count up to B

4x3_root.note: at large B the optimal lines CONSUME THE ENTIRE BUDGET (min = max = B at B=16,24,48,64): optimal play at 4x3 has no capture-count bound independent of B — 'if optimal play never exceeds K captures then B>K is non-binding' is FALSE at 4x3

capture_counts_along_optimal_lines.denominator: root = empty goban, Black to move, budget 0; min/max over optimal (value-achieving) lines; support in the findings JSON of the value mode

longest_games.what_actually_happens: the long lines are capture-and-rebuild wars: White captures 1, Black captures 2, alternating for tens of plies, each player rebuilding the captured stones ('clumping up, filling own eyes, being captured, repeat' — the operator's hypothesis, confirmed literally). The 4x3 B=64 line: 98 plies with the 1,2 rhythm (ply 14..90), then bursts (+4, +2), then double-pass, final board BBBB/BBBB/BW.B = +9, budget exhausted 64/64. Transcripts in the line-mode outputs (untracked/T397-lines/).
longest_games.base_rule_cycles: without the budget the 3x3 graph has 135,512 re-visits in one DFS (the giant SCC per T385: 48,602 of 49,428 vertices) and the 2x2 graph has the T382 7-state capture-exchange cycle; the budget cuts every one of them

scoring_asymmetry.claim: Chinese area scoring is a function of the final board alone, so any capture-and-rebuild round trip is score-neutral; Japanese territory + prisoners is not a board function, so the same round trip is neutral only when the prisoners cancel.
scoring_asymmetry.demo: the T382 2x2 7-state capture-exchange cycle returns to its starting board: area -4 -> -4 (neutral); prisoners 3-3 (balanced, so Japanese also -3 -> -3). Board {B@1,B@3} reached via the cycle (2 B prisoners) vs directly (0 prisoners): area identical (+4), Japanese territory + prisoners 4 vs 2 — differ by exactly the prisoner count.
scoring_asymmetry.why_it_matters: under area scoring the cycling that feels absurd genuinely gains nothing (score-neutral); under territory scoring the same loop is not neutral — which is why the operator's intuition is area-specific

verdict.termination: VERIFIED — the budget game is a DAG; finite without any repetition rule.
verdict.state_cost: cheap — (B+1) table multiplier, one small integer in the key; dense addressing preserved (vs PSK's ban-set explosion).
verdict.hypothesis: PARTIALLY TRUE, and the false half is the finding: the L==H region is preserved at B >= 24 (3x3), but the L<H region's single values are B-dependent and non-convergent (3x3 slots still drift at B=64; the 4x3 root oscillates forever). The budget relocates the bracket's ambiguity into a budget-exhaustion race instead of resolving it.
verdict.recommendation: ruleset investigation only — no ruleset change made (per the bars). If the Orchestrator wants a budget rule, it is a new game and must be declared as one (the MIGOS +2 epitaph); the honest generation deliverable remains the fresh-start single-score region + [L,H] bracket, and the budget does NOT supply the missing single scores the operator hoped for.
